chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): A man performs Tamattu' and forgets to shorten his prayer until he pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj. He said: 'Upon him is a dam (sacrifice) which he must shed.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Dam (sacrifice of an animal as expiation)
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْ: Shortens (prayer from four rak'ahs to two)
key_terms.يُهِلَّ: Pronounces the Talbiyah (entering the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for forgetting to shorten prayers during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who forgets to shorten their prayers during the days of Tashriq before entering Ihram for Haj must offer a *dam* (sacrifice). This ruling highlights the distinction between intentional violation and forgetfulness in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the financial expiation required to rectify the breach of ritual purity before the Hajj rites commence.
